title: Nuevo Laredo Mayor Pitches Border City's Tourism at National Magical Towns Gathering, Deepens Tampico Alliance
excerpt: Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas Villarreal promoted Nuevo Laredo's hunting, medical and business tourism at the National Magical Towns Encounter and highlighted a new alliance with Tampico.
content:
Nuevo Laredo Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas Villarreal took her city's tourism pitch to a national stage this week, joining the Encuentro Nacional de Pueblos Mágicos 2026 to promote the border city as a destination for hunting, medical and business tourism.

The gathering was inaugurated by Tamaulipas Gov. Américo Villarreal Anaya, according to El Congresista, which reported on the mayor's participation. Canturosas Villarreal said the state government is working to position Tamaulipas as a competitive tourism destination, and she pointed to Nuevo Laredo's strengths beyond the Magical Towns program itself.

Among the attractions she highlighted were the city's hunting tourism, medical tourism and commercial and business tourism, along with newer cultural and recreational spaces such as the Museo de Ciencia, Tecnología y Planetario.

The mayor also used the gathering to deepen a strategic alliance with Tampico. Canturosas Villarreal and Tampico Mayor Mónica Villarreal Anaya have agreed to work together to combine the two cities' strengths in logistics and commerce, attract investment and generate new opportunities between northern and southern Tamaulipas, according to the report. Nuevo Laredo is Mexico's leading logistics and customs platform, while Tampico brings a port, commercial and tourism vocation.

"We are strengthening Nuevo Laredo's tourism vocation, which also includes cultural and recreational spaces. It is vital to learn from the experiences of other places to build alliances that move our city forward," the mayor said, according to El Congresista.

The city is also counting down to its holiday season: the municipal newsletter Nuevo Laredo Comunica, dated Nov. 28, promotes the Viveros Mágico 2026 Christmas tree lighting on Dec. 5 at Parque Viveros, with more than 200 illuminated figures.

Sources:

  • El Congresista, Nov. 28, 2026 (with information from Hoy Tamaulipas)
  • Agencia de Noticias Oficina de Corresponsales, Nov. 27, 2026
